structured_output.what_is_happening: HYPERINU ("Hyper Inu") is a generic Pump.fun dog meme token about 44 minutes old. Its self-description is a "shades-on, chain-rocking Solana pup", with no link to any event (https://pump.fun/coin/7vGyP5iCqm6Z9JwMW4wQPVNe1NSpNrM7qej6E8B9pump). In its first hour it traded about $450k of volume from roughly 8.7k buys and 0.9k sells, with about 6,080 unique buyers and 394 unique sellers (packet data from DexScreener and GeckoTerminal). The holder structure is unusually flat: each of the top 10 holders has about 0.30–0.33%. That looks like many wallets buying near-identical sizes, not an organic mix of large and small buyers. Signs of real outside attention are almost absent: GMGN counts 12 page visits, 0 smart-money wallets, 0 KOL wallets and 0 degen calls. My searches found no indexed X, Reddit, news or Telegram discussion. When I re-checked DexScreener at about T2+5 minutes, price was down 13% over the last 5 minutes even though buys still outnumbered sells about 10:1 (https://api.dexscreener.com/latest/dex/tokens/7vGyP5iCqm6Z9JwMW4wQPVNe1NSpNrM7qej6E8B9pump). Many small buys against a few large sells is a common signature of micro-buy or holder-count bots that inflate trending metrics.
